# Cleansia technical audit — 7 October 2026

Status: completed audit and baseline; Phase3 implementation stop.

## Main conclusion and top ten

Start with initial customer data and reliable navigation/session cleanup. The pinned customer SSR build produces a visible hero while its market and catalogue responses fail to decode. Local API hot reads meet the 300 ms server-p95 budget, but paging permits expensive large responses while preventing ordinary navigation beyond offset500. Several measurable byte, allocation, SQL and CI opportunities follow those correctness repairs.

The table ranks work by practical consequence and evidence, rather than treating a score as an automatic implementation order. Impact and likelihood use the same ordinal scale: 1 low, 2 moderate, 3 high. Their product is a comparison aid, not a probability or estimated financial loss. P1 means repair first; P2 means plan an improvement; P3 means lower-priority maintenance. Effort estimates are S up to 1 engineering day, M roughly 1–3 days, L roughly 3–10 days for the cause alone; the costed waves also include regression work and measurement. Actual gains require an approved implementation and a comparable after-run.

Customer laboratory LCP differs sharply between local and DEV (5.276 s versus 1.534 s median), while observed DEV document TTFB exceeds800 ms. Different deployment SHA, hosting, HTTP protocol and fixture prevent treating this as a causal comparison. Hero visibility does not prove catalogue readiness. Native Debug simulator/emulator useful-content medians range from about 0.98 s warm to4.13 s cold; physical-device and DEV-network budgets remain unverified.

Six ranked mobile findings, nine confirmed backend findings, twelve web/delivery findings and one merged documentation finding are retained: 28 ranked findings. Five additional lifecycle, rare-tail and delivery-policy candidates remain unranked. The new delivery candidate records a single required build context shared by four workflows; the intended mandatory roster and actual merge consequences remain unconfirmed. Every card records evidence, counterguards, a proposal and its behavior/API/schema consequences; source-only findings do not receive invented runtime savings.

## Scope and evidence

This audit covers the five API hosts and Functions source, three web apps, two Android apps, two iOS apps and their extensions, authored infrastructure, delivery workflows, local development loops, dependency health and a light correctness/security pass. “Processes” means runtime requests, SQL, background work and external-call boundaries first, then CI and local build/test loops.

Measurements use master snapshot `c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a`, archived outside the Desktop checkout. Source citations refer to that snapshot unless an incremental review explicitly says otherwise. DEV measurements describe the deployed environment and are not assumed to run the same SHA. Authored infrastructure settings are not evidence of deployed settings. No PRO endpoint, SQL, workflow history or Azure CLI operation was used.

Pinned GitHub citations refer to tracked source. The generated Swift SDK `CleansiaCustomerApi/APIs.swift` exists only in the retained scratch build and is labelled as local generated evidence; its inputs and generation commands are retained. It has no invented GitHub permalink. Installed Angular source receipts likewise remain local. The phone copy identifies these local receipts instead of presenting unusable file links.

No application source, API contract or schema was changed. The report is the authorized repository output; the pre-existing `.claude/settings.local.json` change was left alone. No tickets, commits, branches, PRs, deployment or merge was created. No production payment, email, push, geocoding or blob operation was exercised. Isolated background experiments use recording/throw-on-use transports and separate local database clones.

Each retained finding distinguishes measured evidence from reading, names its mechanism and guards, and includes an independent attempt to refute it. Estimates are not before/after gains. A proposed gain must be tested with the same baseline method after its wave is approved. Candidates lacking impact proof are recorded as gaps rather than promoted into confirmed performance problems.

### SQL and physical plans

The normal baseline contains 6,500 HTTP 200 scored requests and 6,500 corresponding server durations, plus 130 excluded warmups. Thirteen paths each have 500 samples across five 100-sequence cohorts. A single persistent HTTP 1.1 connection per scenario and at most eight physical request starts/second keep this a serial warm-process baseline. Ten role identities rotate within the dominant company. The four-call mobile scenario sums are synthetic request sequences, not actual app parallelism or UI time.

The separate instrumented pass contains 130 successful physical requests (ten per path), 1,140 successful EF commands and complete request-duration/SQL scope coverage. SQL counts per request are quote19; customer orders6; admin orders6; partner board15; period pays9; customer-mobile current5, market8, service6, orders6; partner-mobile check3, current2, stats20, preview9. These counts cover those parameter shapes. They do not prove zero growth for larger candidate sets or every mutation. Trace logging was disabled and its original settings verified before startup/jobs.

Retained pg_stat_statements snapshots across the normal window show106,294 per-database statement calls over74 active fingerprints,167,443.75 ms accumulated execution,128,770,860 shared-block hits, zero shared-block reads and zero temporary-block reads/writes. No negative counter deltas were found. These include transaction/connection/background/polling/snapshot work and are not EF command totals or per-endpoint attribution. Zero recorded planning time does not establish zero planning cost. The474 MB database and warmed buffers make this a cache-favourable local baseline; these counters do not describe DEV disk pressure. The offline delta is retained in raw/backend/pg-statements-delta.json.

Fifteen manually reviewed, pure captured SELECTs were replayed five times each in fresh read-only transactions, with exact synthetic bind values, 20 s statement/2 s lock deadlines and rollback. PostgreSQL inferred parameter types for the prepared SELECT; LIMIT became bigint although EF recorded Int32. Fresh first EXECUTE under plan_cache_mode=auto is not proof of a pooled prepared/generic plan. The warmed database and EXPLAIN instrumentation also differ from endpoint timing. Empty package-array and invoice-result samples are explicitly weaker coverage.

These plans support investigating repeated eligibility work if growth warrants it; they do not establish a missing index or a normal-p95 breach. Outer EF projection ORDER BY does not order the inner LIMIT page; the default-sort correctness finding has separate source/UI proof.

### Payload bounds and compression diagnostic

Five valid admin requests each at Limit 20/100/200/10000 produced median client times23.62/37.86/47.60/329.71 ms and bodies63,383/316,704/633,522/about 13.94 MB. The first Limit 100000 request crossed the sampled2 GiB process RSS guard (2,182,064KiB) and its client connection was aborted. It has no valid returned row/body/timing sample and was not repeated. After the client abort, a RequestFinished event reported status200 and 2,974.40 ms of total server request elapsed; this is not client success or an 80,000-row response proof. The sticky post-abort heap and 100 ms RSS sampling also limit peak attribution. Auth, tenant predicates, projections and rate limits remain present.

Five separate gzip-negotiated requests per each of 13 paths (65 total, one fixed identity per path) returned200 without Content-Encoding, Vary, ETag or Cache-Control. Offline gzip6 estimates include admin63,383→2,357 B, partner board60,389→2,061 B, service17,245→3,213 B, customer orders16,020→1,619 B and period pays5,752→705 B. The117 B employee-check body grows to119 B. Synthetic repetition inflates compression ratios; no implementation, production ratio, CPU-throughput gain or end-to-end improvement was measured.

### Startup and local build loop

Five fresh process batches for all five Release API hosts yielded process-to-/alive median 1.842–2.049 s and RSS median 290,160–294,320 KiB, sampled five seconds after all hosts became live. The250 ms probe interval makes readiness an upper-bound observation. PostgreSQL/disk stayed warm. This is neither Azure cold start nor business-content readiness and does not size a shared Azure worker.

Backend forced Release rebuilds (warm NuGet, no restore, no incremental) have two five-run cohorts: median/p90 12.962/28.932 s and 12.428/28.945 s. Unchanged incremental builds are2.470/2.776 s (n5). Each forced build reports219 warning occurrences at 214 unique source positions; the old217 count is superseded. Compiler/cache startup variation is retained rather than described as a stable cold-build baseline. The first29.142 s setup build overlapped tooling setup and is excluded.

Five warmed production web builds skipping Nx result reuse take customer6.067/6.163 s, partner5.616/5.741 s and admin6.281/6.667 s. Angular/dependency/disk caches remain warm. Customer Jest alone takes 4.778/6.346 s (n5), passing279 tests in25 suites; this is narrower than the full workspace. The one npm-ci setup takes 59.072 s. There is no controlled source-edit/watch-loop series.

## Measurement methods and reproducibility

Host: Apple M4, 10 CPU cores, 16 GiB RAM, macOS 15.7.4. Docker Desktop context `desktop-linux`, 10 CPUs and 8.32 GiB VM memory; Colima was also running and was left alone. Benchmark windows were coordinated so browser, native, API and job timings did not compete with deliberate builds or test loops. Normal OS/background activity remains a limitation.

Scratch root: `/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07`. Raw rows, logs, trace artifacts, fixture manifests, helper source and command ledger stay there. Private synthetic sessions/configuration are excluded from publication. Tool/build versions and artifact identities are retained in manifests.

The primary local PostgreSQL 16.15 fixture contains 100,000 orders, 20,000 customers, 500 cleaners and 2,000 recurring templates across three companies, distributed 80/15/5. A 1,000/200/25/50 smoke fixture was checked first. Reference migration/bootstrap/seeds precede synthetic data; foreign-key, crew, pay-row and route-response guards passed. The primary dump precedes authentication writes. Money, addresses, documents and provider identifiers are synthetic; document blobs are placeholders and downloads are excluded. Growth to one million orders was not approved or measured.

The request database is exactly `CleansiaAudit` on loopback port 55432 in the audit-labelled owned container. Five Production-shape Release hosts use isolated content roots, blank optional providers and ports 15000–15004 because AirPlay occupies port 5000. Ordinary application logging is Warning; Hosting Diagnostics timing is Information. This matches authored PRO logging thresholds, not deployed hosting capacity. DEV's authored Cleansia Information threshold differs. SQL/request-body tracing is a separate diagnostic pass and never supplies the normal server-latency baseline.

The fixture intentionally has three companies but the first ten role identities used for primary request repetition belong to the dominant Czech company. Other-company correctness is covered separately by source/tests and isolated job scenarios; no all-market latency claim is made. Deterministic status/user/tenant correlations, future order dates and customer76's cancelled-only orders constrain representativeness.

For an implementation wave days later, recollect the before and after cohorts together on the same current hardware/profile and temporally equivalent restored fixtures. The October7 fixture has absolute dates, and handlers use real UTC; blindly reusing it weeks later can change eligibility and results. Recreate expired synthetic sessions outside scoring, verify row/outcome guards for both versions, and retain the same relative-date distribution. The retained October7 results are a historical baseline, not an automatic counterfactual for a later master revision. Keep the dormant-provider simulator profile for those paired comparisons; physical devices and live-provider profiles require their own baseline.

API/SQL/job details and exact artifact methods follow below.

Web: production artifacts, retained esbuild metafiles and gzip size attribution. Repeated builds bypass Nx result reuse but retain warm Angular/dependency/disk caches. Browser/Lighthouse scenarios name language preference, cookies, cold HTTP cache, SSR route and authentication explicitly. The corrected Lighthouse Czech scenario uses a saved site preference so SSR and hydrated text agree. Lighthouse simulated slow 4G/4× CPU metrics are separate from observed desktop trace timing and from field Core Web Vitals. Anonymous DEV traffic is light; authenticated fixture screens are local. DEV admin's perimeter restriction is recorded rather than bypassed.

Native: all four applications have ten process-cold and ten warm runs in signed-out and signed-in conditions (160 retained runs). Cold termination preserves conditioned login/preferences/data/cache; warm backgrounds for one second and resumes. Notification permission is denied. iOS uses a dedicated iPhone16/iOS 18.6 simulator under Xcode26.3 and scoped ad hoc simulator entitlements; Android uses a fresh scratch Pixel8/API 35 guest. Existing owner devices/AVDs are not reset. These are Debug builds; paid/device distribution and TestFlight were not invoked. iOS useful boundaries and Android's progressive stats boundary differ and are labelled.

Existing test counts/times, mobile supplemental outcomes and historical CI envelopes follow below.

Percentiles use nearest-rank p90; median uses the ordinary even-sample median. Small n5/n10 percentiles are descriptive. API p95 is reported with its successful sample count and request-to-server-log coverage. Failed setup, signing, selector, locale and proxy diagnostics are retained and excluded with reasons; no successful subset of an interrupted cohort is silently treated as a passing complete cohort.

## Backend jobs tests and detailed findings

Backend measurement/audit input for the Phase3 report. Source remained pinned and unchanged; all runtime work used disposable local synthetic fixtures. Main API/SQL/startup/build/CI tables are in root-baselines-section.md; this section supplies jobs, tests and guarded findings.

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|

| cleanup | 1000 old pending card checkouts cancelled | 2133.539 | 2173.582 | 1010 |
| recurring | 2000 templates processed/1450 occurrences created/0 failed | 19325.915 | 19514.925 | 52224 |

Each mutation sample restores its own prepared snapshot. Zero external attempts and exact row/result gates passed. Existing UTC handlers and core commands unchanged; recording queue substitutes transport. Fresh-process lazy DI/JIT and successful-query hashing are included; model/count setup, restore, Functions trigger lease and external network are excluded. SQL counts omit failed/synchronous commands. Post-count RSS includes setup; macOS PeakWorkingSet64=0 is unavailable, not zero memory use. Five-run p90 is the maximum. The digest fixture proves a bounded mechanism rather than a500-cleaner production cost.

Logging allocation evidence: logging-allocation-summary.json pairs all five actual compiled middleware with an identical direct delegate for each method/response size, five×100 awaited samples, NullLogger, no forcedGC. Stopwatch elapsed medians of run medians cannot be labelled CPU time or HTTP/server time. NullLogger disables Warning/Error too; any implementation must preserve authoredPRO Warning/Error body observability and redaction. Larger-payload gzip6 byte savings remain untimed estimates; actual65 negotiated replies were uncompressed. The100000-row profile was halted after one invalid client sample above 2 GiB observed RSS and has no completed cohort latency/body/row count.

Findings and decisions:


#### B001 — Whole response buffering and large character buffers remain active when logging is disabled (P2, 2 impact × 3 likelihood; M effort).

measured-local-optimization-opportunity.


**Reachable trigger:** Any ordinary API request on all five hosts; excluded health/swagger paths bypass the middleware. Successful 200 responses still enter request and response body reads even with NullLogger.

The middleware always buffers the full response and calls two bounded body reads; each allocates char[65537] even when Information is disabled. The actual compiled five-host diagnostic measures275358–1451064 B additional allocation per request versus the identical direct delegate across GET/POST and 1 KiB/64 KiB/1 MiB responses. These are local in-process elapsed/allocation measurements, not measured CPU time, HTTP latency or a production GC incident.

**Guard qualification:** SafeBody suppresses bodies over 64Ki characters and redacts before truncation; these privacy guards are real and must remain.; ReadBoundedAsync bounds each read but allocates char[65537] on each invocation.; Response MemoryStream captures the entire produced response before reading/copying; no ILogger.IsEnabled gate found in any host copy.


**Independent skeptic/refutation:** Root independently checked every compiled allocation row, exact output bytes and paired body/method baselines. Disabled Information does not disable unconditional capture; production Warning/Error preservation limits the proposed fast path. [skeptic-backend-bounds-logging-compression-root.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/audit/skeptic-backend-bounds-logging-compression-root.json) (reviewed).


**Proposal:** Use bounded capture with stream forwarding and a disabled-level fast path where observability permits it; avoid formatting request bodies when Information is disabled. Preserve authoredPRO Warning/Error response and exception body observability, redaction and oversized-body suppression across all five hosts.


**Expected gain:** The measured paired excess allocation is 275358–1451064 B/request depending on method and payload. A bounded implementation can reduce it, but retained Warning/Error capture, after-change allocation, HTTPp95 and production GC savings must be measured. [estimate-not-benchmark].


**Risk/contract:** Medium: middleware ordering, streaming/error responses and PII suppression must retain behavior. Behavior: none API: none Schema: none.

#### B002 — Shared offset ceiling prevents ordinary navigation after offset 500 (P2, 2 impact × 3 likelihood; S effort).

runtime-confirmed-functional-finding.


**Reachable trigger:** Shared validation rejects offsets above 500. Actual synthetic admin UI diagnostic advertised 80000 company orders; clicking last page 4000 sent Offset=79980&Limit=20, returned HTTP 400 and retained the previous 20 table rows while the counter advanced to 79981–80000 of 80000.

Offset is limited to 0..500 although paged responses can advertise much larger totals; ordinary later pages cannot be requested.

**Guard qualification:** Current authorization and tenant scoping permit legitimate admin order reads; invalid DataRange request is rejected by model/validator checks.; Do not use employee-list volume as the reproduction: 500 total cleaners split across companies may not exceed 520 for one admin.


**Independent skeptic/refutation:** Root independently checked the actual UI400 and retained table rows. Inclusive offset500 and company volume guards were challenged; the 80k admin fixture reaches the rejected advertised page. [skeptic-backend-pagination.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/audit/skeptic-backend-pagination.json) (reviewed).


**Proposal:** Agree maximum depth/cursor policy and align API validation and UI paginator. Preserve non-negative validation and enforce a small page-size ceiling separately.


**Expected gain:** Correct navigation through the advertised records; no performance gain claimed. [estimate-not-benchmark].


**Risk/contract:** Low to medium: shared DTO affects many endpoints and clients. Behavior: Offset validation behavior changes; decide backwards-compatible paging contract. API: Offset validation behavior changes; decide backwards-compatible paging contract. Schema: none.


**Source:** [src/Cleansia.Core.AppServices/Shared/DTOs/RequestModels/DataRangeRequest.cs:11](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/src/Cleansia.Core.AppServices/Shared/DTOs/RequestModels/DataRangeRequest.cs#L11), [src/Cleansia.Core.AppServices/Behaviors/ValidationPipelineBehavior.cs:88](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/src/Cleansia.Core.AppServices/Behaviors/ValidationPipelineBehavior.cs#L88)


**Evidence:** [samples.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/web/waterfalls/diagnostic-admin-pagination-v3/samples.json), [skeptic-backend-pagination.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/audit/skeptic-backend-pagination.json)



#### B003 — Authenticated pages accept a request for 100000 rows (P2, 2 impact × 3 likelihood; S effort).

measured-local-optimization-opportunity.


**Reachable trigger:** Legitimate admin calls AdminOrder/get-paged with Limit=100000; tenant bounds rows to the admin company but the primary fixture has 80000 matching orders.

The shared ceiling allows many orders and nested projected children to materialize and serialize in one response; logging B001 may add a separate copy. This is a distinct row-bound cause. Five valid reads at each limit20/100/200/10000 show payload and memory growth; the first100000-limit request was halted by the 2 GiB RSS guard at 2182064 KiB and produced no accepted client timing/body/row count.

**Guard qualification:** Authorization, tenant filters, per-sub rate limiter and server-side projection are present.; Fixed SQL statement count does not bound rows/materialization/JSON/response buffering.; No DoS or p95 violation asserted without isolated broad-page measurement.


**Independent skeptic/refutation:** Root checked authenticated row/tenant/rate/projection guards and the bounded page matrix. The first100000 request crossed the RSS guard; its incomplete client sample cannot establish returned rows, successful latency or DoS. [skeptic-backend-bounds-logging-compression-root.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/audit/skeptic-backend-bounds-logging-compression-root.json) (reviewed).


**Proposal:** Choose an evidence-backed interactive ceiling (candidate 100 or 200); give exports a separate streaming or batched path when the business needs all rows. Keep offset/cursor decision separate from page size.


**Expected gain:** An agreed interactive ceiling bounds rows, payload and materialization; measured page20/100/200/10000 payload growth supports that decision. After-change memory and latency savings remain unmeasured; the 100000 case is one guard-aborted diagnostic. [estimate-not-benchmark].

#### B011 — Default order pages apply LIMIT before any deterministic database ordering (P2, 2 impact × 2 likelihood; S effort).

source-and-runtime-SQL-confirmed-correctness-finding.


**Reachable trigger:** Actual default admin/customer/partner Available UI requests omit Sort. Existing waterfall receipts show10 admin,10 customer and 10 Available reads; My orders supplies its own sort. Captured successful SQL confirms an unordered inner LIMIT/OFFSET subquery.

Null Sort maps to an empty enumerable, and the repository applies Skip/Take without constructing a sorter. Database physical order can define page membership; EF split queries cannot establish a stable unique ordering from the outer grouping sort.

**Guard qualification:** OrderSort.DefaultSort=CreatedOn is a real fallback only after a BaseSort instance is constructed; zero sort definitions skip the loop entirely.; Outer ORDER BY on projected parent/child IDs groups the returned page but does not define membership before inner LIMIT.; Explicit My orders/client sort guards one path. Ordinary nonunique sorts also need a unique tie-breaker before paging.; No missing/duplicate record incident or latency consequence was reproduced. Offset ceiling B002 is a separate validation defect.


**Independent skeptic/refutation:** Root checked default sorter guards against actual unordered innerLIMIT SQL and 40 real UI requests. Explicit-sort MyOrders refutes a universal claim; no missing or duplicate records were reproduced. [skeptic-backend-query-order.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/audit/skeptic-backend-query-order.json) (reviewed).


**Proposal:** Agree the product default order per list, apply it before Skip/Take for an empty sort collection and append a unique Id tie-breaker for all page orders. Preserve currency-leading monetary sort behavior.


**Expected gain:** Stable and predictable page membership; no performance gain claimed. [estimate-not-benchmark].


**Risk/contract:** Medium: visible default order changes and shared repository surface need compatible per-list choices. Behavior: Default ordering changes, DTO/schema unchanged. API: Default ordering changes, DTO/schema unchanged. Schema: none.

Targets are localhost audit ports 4000,4310–4312,15000–15004 and the exact DEV hosts enumerated in egress-process.json. An explicit loopback HTTP/CONNECT allowlist proxy restricts host+port, including literal IPs, while preserving browser HTTP cache. DNS rules are additional guard only. This is browser HTTP/CONNECT target isolation, not complete machine egress isolation. Chrome background Google hosts were denied; no public CDN font requests were required because fonts are self-hosted.

The customer SSR production host is on :4000, forwarded by :4310; local API targets come from raw/backend/hosts-state.json. Browser and SSR use the same absolute http://localhost:4310 API base to preserve native transfer-cache keys. No artificial duplicate-fetch finding was retained from prior scratch URL misalignment.

### Proposed wave order and owner decisions

1. Correct initial data readiness first: W07(M), separately committed from backend paging/ordering causes. Restore both Node decoding and JSON-safe cache transport before repeating coherent data-ready CWV measurements. Gain is intended behavior restored; latency gain unknown.

[GitHub identifies workflow checks by job name and does not distinguish workflow, matrix or event types](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/troubleshooting-rules). [GitHub recommends distinct job names across workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches), because duplicate names can make required results ambiguous. The current configuration establishes the context name, rather than that every historical workflow is independently required. CI wall-time summaries remain descriptive until the selected check identity is unambiguous. [GitHub's branch-rules endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules#get-rules-for-a-branch) covers active applicable rules at all configured levels and excludes evaluate/disabled rulesets; the captured listing was complete.

**Proposal and scope.** Agree mandatory checks by PR class, assign distinct stable emitted job names, and update hosted selectors deliberately under owner approval. Any chosen aggregate gate must always run and evaluate the intended conditional jobs. Renaming source jobs without changing selectors, or automatically requiring every path-scoped job, can block merging; [GitHub documents filtering-related pending required checks](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks). No source or hosted-rule change occurred in this audit.

**Estimate, effort and risk.** Expected gain is unmeasured operational clarity and gate reliability; no seconds, runner savings or probability are promised. S for roster/name design and narrowly approved selectors; an aggregate policy can expand to M and needs separate scope agreement. Moderate CI operational risk. Behavior: CI merge-gate semantics may change and require owner approval. API: none. Schema: none. This candidate is outside the ranked list and has not been added to final web JSON.

### Environment, data and measurement boundaries

Measurements ran serially on owned fresh guests: iPhone 16/iOS 18.6 (22G86), UUID `AA44A365-C04D-4EA2-907E-EB8E66623426`; Pixel 8 profile/API 35 Google APIs arm64-v8a, software GPU, 2 GiB RAM, four guest cores, configured 60 Hz, serial `emulator-5580`. The host is an Apple M4 MacBook Air with 16 GiB RAM, macOS 15.7.4 (24G517), Xcode 26.3 (17C529), explicit JDK 21, Docker Desktop allocated 8 GiB and Colima running. Setup builds overlapped backend fixture preparation and are not uncontended compiler benchmarks. During retained mobile launches, other lanes performed read-only work without heavy builds/API load/restarts. Owner guests were untouched. All owned guests and the local observer stopped at 10:49 UTC.

Both platforms used Debug artifacts with dormant external SDK configuration. Android manifest overlays disable Firebase auto-init/collection and remove FirebaseInitProvider; runtime Mapbox, Sentry, Google and Stripe keys are blank. iOS has no GoogleService-Info.plist, blank optional keys, no APS entitlement and no Apple sign-in capability in its scratch simulator configuration. Final iOS artifacts use Xcode Sign to Run Locally (`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=-`, simulator-only `AUDIT00000` identity); valid simulator application identifiers restore normal Keychain persistence. No account/certificate provisioning, physical device, TestFlight or production access occurred. This configuration is not equivalent to shipping Release with live provider integrations.

Synthetic localhost data contains 100,000 orders, 20,000 customers, 500 cleaners and 2,000 templates. Customer-76 was selected from the existing fixture because its cancelled orders avoid the completed-order review/map flow; its loaded first-viewport address is `Synthetic audit street 76`. Partner-1 is eligible with an approved profile, complete registration/documents/consents and a synthetic legacy IBAN satisfying the existing presence gate. No review, payout, blob/media or fixture-order mutation was performed. Native auth/device conditioning used the intended local flow; this is not a claim of zero auth-session database writes. Fixture selection is recorded in [fixture-selection.json](/Users/michael/.codex/scratchpads/cleansia-audit-2026-10-07/raw/mobile/fixture-selection.json).

Process-cold terminates the application while retaining conditioned session/onboarding/preferences and disk caches; it is not a reboot or empty-filesystem launch. Warm resume keeps the process alive and backgrounds it for one second; it does not validate a stale-cache resume beyond TTL. The English locale and denied notification permission profile are held fixed. Signed-out readiness requires the real editable sign-in form and recovery/navigation controls. Customer signed-in readiness requires the visible loaded saved-address control; partner readiness requires loaded Dashboard stats and the legitimate next-job/available-work/empty state. Other Home requests may continue afterward; Android partner upcoming orders/available preview may also finish after the stats boundary.

The observational proxy binds only 127.0.0.1:16002/16004 and forwards to local mobile hosts 15002/15004. Customer iOS cold runs have 17 requests, mostly overlapping; GetPlans repeats twice with 617 bytes per body. A deliberate 1.8-second branded hold explains the roughly 1.91-second Market-to-next-wave gap in a retained sample. Changing that hold is an explicit owner behavior decision. The 1.5-second Home first-paint fallback ceiling also refutes an unbounded global-loading assertion. Partner iOS employee identity is a genuine Stats input; the independent preview is awaited afterward before loaded state. In the retained ten cold runs, median observed Stats and Preview request durations are 110.5 ms and 140.3 ms respectively. Android publishes Stats progressively; upcoming orders then delay starting an independent preview, so the measured Stats readiness is not full-preview completion. None of these observations establishes an after-change saving.

#### MOB-S11-01 — iOS partner checklist persistence is outside the session-wipe set

**Classification:** P2; source status `source_confirmed`; area iOS partner / S11; severity Medium; evidence kind `reading_and_scratch_characterization`.

**Impact × likelihood score:** 2 (moderate) × 2 (moderate) = 4; P2. Actual isolated production checklist store retains a synthetic tick after normal/terminal session teardown; source omission is confirmed. Order-ID keying and no subsequent-account UI disclosure test limit the moderate impact claim.

**Impact / likelihood:** Prior cleaner checklist identifiers and ticks survive logout on disk. Deterministic persistence; visible crossover requires the next account to open the same order.

**Mechanism:** The long-lived store writes `order_checklist.<orderId>` arrays to standard UserDefaults. It neither conforms to SessionScopedCache nor exposes a wipe, while the production registry omits it. Normal logout and refresh-terminal logout therefore do not reach those keys.

#### MOB-S11-04 — Android private-image caches have no visible session clear

**Classification:** Unresolved candidate; not promoted; source status `candidate_requires_characterization`; area Android customer/partner / S11; severity Medium potential; evidence kind `reading`.

**Impact × likelihood score:** 2 (moderate) × 2 (moderate) = 4; Potential only; unranked, actual exposure/frequency unverified. Potential-only conditional score: private-image/SAS cache retention would have moderate impact after a viewed cacheable image. No private image/cache artifact was observed; installed-policy receipts alone do not confirm retention or frequency.

**Impact / likelihood:** Potential retention of private image bytes/SAS URLs across sessions. Requires a viewed remote private image; baseline avatars are null and no blob requests ran.

**Mechanism:** Both applications own a singleton Coil ImageLoader. No source call clears its memory/disk caches on session end. Customer thumbnails/fullscreen/evidence use raw URLs or ImageRequest without disabling disk cache; partner job thumbnails explicitly disable disk cache. Declared and cached Coil version is 3.0.4. Its tagged primary implementation enables disk policy, creates singletonDiskCache, and default cache strategy writes response body and metadata without Cache-Control checks. Backend SAS explicitly serves private,max-age=3600, which is not no-store. Actual synthetic on-disk retention still needs characterization. Policy sources: [Coil3.0.4 disk cache enabled by default](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.0.4/coil-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/request/ImageRequest.kt#L206-L212); [Coil3.0.4 singletonDiskCache default](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.0.4/coil-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/ImageLoader.kt#L286-L298); [Coil3.0.4 default strategy writes bodies and metadata](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.0.4/coil-network-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/network/internal/utils.kt#L59-L83); [NetworkFetcher applies write policy and cache strategy](https://github.com/coil-kt/coil/blob/3.0.4/coil-network-core/src/commonMain/kotlin/coil3/network/NetworkFetcher.kt#L115-L141).

Deduplicate per market/session, preserve explicit refresh.

### S11 membership, all three triggers, extensions and allowlist

The source contract at [security-rules.md:755–789](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/security-rules.md#L755) covers every long-lived per-user value, persisted row and freshness watermark. Registry participation alone is not proof that in-flight producers cannot repopulate a cleared holder. The iOS weak registry takes a locked snapshot and awaits clears, without cancelling producers. Existing injected-set auth tests are not a production roster-equality gate; no maintained roster assertion or CI gate was added.

| App | Declared production members | Roster |
| --- | --- | --- |
| android customer | 12 | AddressRepository; OrderRepository; DisputeRepository; LoyaltyRepository; ReferralRepository; MembershipRepository; RecurringBookingRepository; PushTokenRepository; UserRepository; NotificationPreferencesRepository; NotificationFeedRepository; SavedCardRepository |
| android partner | 8 | OrdersRepositoryImpl; ProfileRepositoryImpl; DashboardRepositoryImpl; InvoicesRepositoryImpl; OrderChecklistRepository; UserProfileStore; PushTokenRepository; NotificationFeedRepository |
| ios customer | 11 | OrderRepository; LoyaltyRepository; RewardsReferralRepository; MembershipRepository; RecurringBookingRepository; DisputeRepository; SavedAddressRepository; UserProfileRepository; RemoteImageCache (avatar); NotificationBadgeModel; PushTokenRegistrar |
| ios partner | 7 | LivePartnerProfileClient (stateless clear); LivePartnerDevicesClient (stateless clear); OrdersStaleness; InvoicesStaleness; PendingOffersStore; NotificationBadgeModel; PushTokenRegistrar |

Android customer voluntary logout, terminal refresh rejection and successful customer deletion each iterate the injected session-cache set; deletion uses Provider to break the self-referential graph. Android partner voluntary/terminal logout iterate its set; the partner deletion button is an admin request and intentionally does not terminate the session. iOS voluntary logout reaches signOutLocal (token clear, then registry clear); terminal SessionRefresher rejection clears the registry/tokens and emits forced sign-out; successful customer deletion calls signOutLocal. Partner iOS deletion remains an admin request under ADR-0052. An eventual revoked/deleted partner session follows the terminal-refresh path. Source trigger receipts are listed below.

No app-group per-user snapshot file was found. Notification-service and Live Activity extensions read the device-level inAppLanguageTag, which belongs on the retained device-preference side. ActivityKit cards are OS-owned content and require their own session teardown; clearing an app group does not substitute for ending them. The existing order-identity/adoption and backend ownership checks are retained as counterguards.

```text
3: /// Local-only persistence for the cleaner's checklist ticks, keyed by orderId.
4: /// PURELY LOCAL — there is no backend checklist API; the ticks are the cleaner's

8:     func checkedIds(orderId: String) -> Set<String>
9:     func setChecked(orderId: String, itemId: String, checked: Bool)
10: }

17:         self.defaults = defaults

21:         let stored = defaults.stringArray(forKey: key(orderId)) ?? []
22:         return Set(stored)

30:             ids.remove(itemId)
```

```text
755: ## S11 — Every per-user cache on mobile is wiped on session end (shared-device leak)
756: 
757: **On a shared device, the previous user's cached data must NOT survive to the next account.** ANY
758: mobile `@Singleton` (Android) / long-lived injected class (iOS) that holds **per-user state** — a
759: cached `StateFlow`/`@Published`, a persistent DataStore/`UserDefaults` row, a
760: [`Staleness`](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/master/src/cleansia_android/core/src/main/java/cz/cleansia/core/freshness/Staleness.kt)
761: watermark, or a per-key `Map` of any of these — **is a member of the session-wipe set and must be
762: flushed on session end.** Leaving one out leaks the prior user's orders / profile / invoices /
763: notifications to the next account on that handset — a security defect, not a UX nit (this rule was
764: authored after the class recurred 5+ times: `PushTokenRepository`, `NotificationFeedCache`,
765: `UserProfileStore`, customer `UserRepository`, and the T-0416 stragglers Dashboard/Orders/Invoices/
766: Profile/OrderChecklist/NotificationPreferences).
767: 
768: **The mechanism (single source of truth, never a hand-maintained clear-list):**
769: - **Android** — implement `cz.cleansia.core.auth.SessionScopedCache` and join the Hilt multibinding
770:   (`@Binds @IntoSet … : SessionScopedCache` in the app's `SessionScopedModule` / feature module). The
771:   auth layer iterates `Set<SessionScopedCache>` on every wipe path.
772: - **iOS** — conform to `SessionScopedCache` and `register(self)` with the injected
773:   `SessionScopedCacheRegistry` (held weakly); `clearAll()` iterates it.
774: 
775: **Three wipe-triggers, one set — they must not drift.** The set is iterated on **all three**:
776: 1. **Sign-out** (voluntary `logout()`),
777: 2. **Authenticator forced-401** (the refresh-terminal path — a revoked/reset session),
778: 3. **Account deletion** (customer `UserRepository.deleteAccount()` — which, being itself a member,
779:    injects `Provider<Set<@JvmSuppressWildcards SessionScopedCache>>` / iterates the registry to
780:    break the self-referential Dagger cycle).
781: 
782: **The allowlist (the only sanctioned exception).** A `@Singleton` that holds cached state but whose
783: state is **device-level or public, not per-user**, is legitimately out of the set — but only if it is
784: on the **named, reason-annotated allowlist** in [`consistency.md` §E9](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/master/agents/knowledge/consistency.md) /
785: [`patterns-mobile.md`](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/master/agents/knowledge/patterns-mobile.md). A stateless pass-through (no cache field) is trivially
786: out and needs no allowlist entry, but should carry a one-line `// Stateless — nothing cached, so no
787: SessionScopedCache` comment (as `DeviceManagementRepository` does) so a reviewer isn't left guessing.
788: **A per-user holder missing from both the set and the allowlist is an S11 violation** — caught today by
789: the Reviewer (reading the diff + the `check-consistency.mjs` E9 warn-only advisory); the mechanical hard
```

```text
155:     override suspend fun refresh(employeeId: String?, force: Boolean): ApiError? {
156:         refreshLock.withLock {
157:             val fresh = _snapshot.value.loaded && !staleness.isStale(STALE_WINDOW_MS)
158:             if (fresh && !force) return null
159: 
160:             _snapshot.update { it.copy(refreshing = true) }
161:             var firstError: ApiError? = null
162: 
163:             when (val statsResult = getStats(employeeId)) {
164:                 is ApiResult.Success -> _snapshot.update { it.copy(stats = statsResult.data) }
165:                 is ApiResult.Error -> firstError = statsResult.error
166:             }
167: 
168:             if (!employeeId.isNullOrBlank()) {
169:                 when (val upcoming = getUpcomingOrders(employeeId, 10)) {
170:                     is ApiResult.Success -> _snapshot.update { it.copy(upcoming = upcoming.data) }
171:                     is ApiResult.Error -> { /* non-critical — keep dashboard usable */ }
172:                 }
173:             } else {
174:                 _snapshot.update { it.copy(upcoming = emptyList()) }
175:             }
176: 
177:             when (val preview = getAvailableJobsPreview(5)) {
178:                 is ApiResult.Success -> _snapshot.update { it.copy(availableJobsPreview = preview.data) }
179:                 is ApiResult.Error -> { /* non-critical */ }
180:             }
181: 
182:             // Mark fresh even when non-critical sub-calls fail — stats is
183:             // the load-bearing call, and the snapshot already preserves
184:             // last-known-good values for the optional sections. If even
185:             // stats failed, firstError surfaces and the caller can react,
186:             // but we still stamp so we don't hammer the network on every
187:             // resume; the next user pull will force-bypass anyway.
188:             staleness.markFresh()
189:             _snapshot.update { it.copy(loaded = true, refreshing = false) }
190:             return firstError
191:         }
192:     }
```

## Infrastructure security dependency and documentation coverage

### Infrastructure and security coverage

Infrastructure was reviewed from authored Bicep, without Azure CLI or deployed-state inspection. DEV uses the shared B2 plan and PostgreSQL Burstable B1 ms. Authored PRO uses the shared S1 plan, PostgreSQL GeneralPurpose D2s_v3, zonal high availability, 35-day geo-redundant backup and ZRS storage. Five API processes, customer SSR and Functions share the application plan. The explicit API/SSR/Functions Always On settings override module defaults; staging disables it deliberately. API probes use `/alive`, SSR `/health`, and Functions `/api/health`.

DEV is authored as one fixed instance. Authored PRO CPU autoscaling uses 70% for scale-out, 30% for scale-in and one to three instances. TLS, private networking, managed storage identity and least-privilege database controls were checked in source. Public blob endpoints support signed URLs while containers disallow public anonymous access. No CDN/Front Door declaration was found. These are source facts, not confirmation of deployed configuration or sufficient worker capacity. Local process RSS cannot determine Azure Linux capacity, and no infrastructure defect is retained solely from a SKU, module default or CPU-only scaling.

The light S1–S12 review checked authenticated subject ownership, route authorization/anonymous rosters, guest live-token pins, PII redaction, named rate policies, redaction-before-truncation and body suppression, financial idempotency/transaction boundaries, tenant filters and explicit bypass constraints, initial migration/least-privilege declarations, consumer-specific active predicates, mobile session wipes and upload/served-content guards. The source ledger is `raw/audit/root-security-infra.json`; existing backend unit/integration/host test execution is reported separately. This is coverage evidence, not a blanket security certification.

Important refutations: a normal request tenant provider is registered; design-time provider absence is intentional. Tenantless reads fail closed to null-tenant envelopes. Partner payroll controllers are GET-only; the Admin payroll/invoice mutations explicitly use auth rate limits. Documented S7b local flushes, per-tenant commits and unique-race handling are not mechanical CQRS violations. A public blob endpoint is not a public container. Missing future guards are risks to investigate, not present exploit proof.

### D-01 — operating documentation preserves superseded facts

P3, impact 1 (low) × likelihood 3 (high) = 3; reading, independently checked. Security/setup readers can follow the wrong tenant authorization explanation or superseded approval guidance. The source and documentation disagree at [docs/architecture/security-rules.md:234](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/security-rules.md#L234) (anonymous filter bypass), `:328` (Partner payroll rate-limit gap), `:733` (owner-only generation/schema execution), [CLAUDE.md:100](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/CLAUDE.md#L100) (framework versions), `:301` (NSwag instruction), and [docs/architecture/infrastructure.md:757](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/infrastructure.md#L757) (readiness probes). The newer infrastructure explanation at `:520` and current owner's DEV deployment/reset restrictions still apply.

[deploy/bicep/main.bicep:593](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/deploy/bicep/main.bicep#L593) also claims DEV's Cleansia Information prefix excludes request-body logging. All five middleware use `ILogger<RequestLoggingMiddleware>` in `Cleansia.Web.*`, so `:597` admits those Information events; [docs/architecture/request-logging.md:56](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/request-logging.md#L56) already says so. Successful Information logs are suppressed by authored PRO's Warning threshold, while Warning/Error responses remain admitted. Redaction guards are intact; no deployed-state or privacy exploit is asserted. Web finding W-05 is merged into this cause, including [docs/architecture/frontend.md:3](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/frontend.md#L3) and the obsolete frontend timing comment.

Proposed fix: reconcile these cited facts with current source and owner rules, without introducing a new policy or gate. Expected gain is clearer setup/investigation; time saving is unmeasured. Effort S, low risk, no behavior/API/schema change. Skeptic checks matched the registered tenant guard, GET/mutation action rosters, Bicep overrides, health paths and logging category prefix; older notes do not override this audit's no-PRO and DEV approval rules.

### Tooling and dependency qualifications

The graphify-not-installed hypothesis is refuted: the pipx executable and rebuild function exist. The documented default `python3` import is unavailable in that interpreter. No application code was edited, so CLAUDE's code-change rebuild trigger does not apply; stale graph reports were navigation aids only. Docker Desktop and Colima were both running, and the audit used the existing Docker Desktop context without touching Colima containers/volumes.

Only Dependabot alert 279 was open when the authorized repository alert read ran. Its `http-cache-semantics` advisory has no patched version listed; measured browser/SSR metafiles do not include that dependency. Development dependency status alone is insufficient exploit evidence. The test-only SQLite audit suppression matches its no-patch advisory; none of the five compiled API dependency manifests contains SQLite. No deployed application vulnerability follows from those facts.

The upcoming Nx 24 change removes the deprecated built-in Jest/ESLint executors, while the executor API and Angular executors are outside that removal. Current Nx 23.1.2 is functional. The `ubuntu-latest` rollout is gradual from 19 October to 19 November 2026; current sampled runs use Ubuntu24.04. These are future compatibility tasks, not observed present breakage. Primary sources: [Nx announcement](https://nx.dev/blog/look-mum-no-executors), [GitHub runner migration](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-17-ubuntu-26-generally-available-and-latest-migration/), [http-cache-semantics advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp), [SQLite advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q).

Independent skeptic receipt: `raw/audit/skeptic-root-report-web.json`; exact security/infrastructure source guards are retained in `raw/audit/root-security-infra.json`.

D-01 source anchors: [docs/architecture/security-rules.md:234](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/security-rules.md#L234), [docs/architecture/security-rules.md:328](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/security-rules.md#L328), [docs/architecture/security-rules.md:733](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/security-rules.md#L733), [CLAUDE.md:100](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/CLAUDE.md#L100), [CLAUDE.md:301](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/CLAUDE.md#L301), [docs/architecture/infrastructure.md:757](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/docs/architecture/infrastructure.md#L757), [deploy/bicep/main.bicep:593](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/deploy/bicep/main.bicep#L593).

**S6 logging scope.** Authored DEV's Cleansia Information category admits the request middleware's Information events; authored PRO's Warning threshold suppresses successful Information events and retains Warning/Error responses. Redaction remains relevant. No deployed-state or privacy-exploit claim follows from that category correction; it is part of D-01. The corrected suppression bound is characters, as the source explicitly documents.

**S7 transaction boundary.** [UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/src/Cleansia.Core.AppServices/Behaviors/UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior.cs#L20) commits successful command results and rolls back failures; it does not by itself open an encompassing database transaction. [CleanupStalePendingOrders](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/src/Cleansia.Core.AppServices/Features/Orders/CleanupStalePendingOrders.cs#L155) commits tracked cancellation/history/feed/outbox changes per tenant. [CreditAccountRepository](https://github.com/VM-s-Solutions/cleansia/blob/c66a03168d3810d79299dfca48688bf7168d814a/src/Cleansia.Infra.Database/Repositories/CreditAccountRepository.cs#L107) can commit a positive credit return in its own transaction when neither a current nor ambient transaction exists. The measured B006 fixture used zero credit and does not prove joint credit/cancellation atomicity. A batching proposal must preserve the current idempotency and failure boundary, or make any changed boundary a concrete owner decision; this table introduces no new credit defect.

Existing shared auth/cache tests do not replace an account-switch or OS-extension disclosure experiment. No APNs workload or physical-device claim is introduced.

## Roadmap and owner decisions

These are planning estimates for one engineer, including focused regression, relevant full verification and comparable after-measurement. Review/CI waiting, physical-device access and provider provisioning add elapsed time. The ranges are uncertain until each selected wave receives a narrow implementation scope. No wave is approved by this report, and no backlog ticket has been filed.

| Wave | Causes and concrete scope | Estimated cost | Expected gain and acceptance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| A Correctness first | W-07 customer SSR decoding/cache; B002/B003/B011 paging bounds, navigation and deterministic ordering; MOB-S11-01 checklist and MOB-S11-03 Live Activity teardown | 4–7 engineering days | Initial nonempty catalogue and reliable page/session state. Assert actual hydrated DTOs, deep-page behavior and teardown. Pagination policy/default ordering need owner choices; do not silently break TestFlight 13 or alter currency-leading money order. New cursor/export functionality is excluded from this cost and requires separate scope approval |
| B Small byte and read wins | W-06 original-preserving responsive mascot; W-02 lazy charts; W-03 one animation provider; W-08 lazy notification page; B004 one validator-owned lookup, preserving the separate handler tracked/current read; D-01 documentation alignment; MOB-REL-01 concurrency warning repair | 3–5 engineering days | Lower initial bytes, eliminate3 repeated validator reads (their observed SQL median totals2.171ms), and resolve three Swift language-mode warnings. No LCP/build saving is promised; same artifact/browser/build methods decide the result |
| C Request and native startup work | B001 logging allocation/capture; B009 application response compression; MOB-PERF-01 native parallel independent reads; MOB-PERF-02 duplicate plan single-flight/cache | 3–5 engineering days | Reduce paired allocations/wire bytes and serial waiting, with measured after-values. Keep Warning/Error capture/redaction, cache/auth policy, cancellation and exact DTO/status behavior. Compression CPU/secret-response policy needs assessment; tiny117 B body need not be compressed |
| D Jobs and query growth | B005 digest overlap reads; B006 bounded stale-checkout sweep; B010 correlated seat-count simplification | 4–7 engineering days | Fewer SQL commands/materialized rows at fixed outcomes and fixture scale. Keep half-open overlaps, watermarks, tenant boundaries, unique occurrence/seat guards and credit idempotency. Preserve tracked tenant failure boundaries or obtain explicit approval before changing commit semantics |
| E Delivery and local loop | C-01/C-02 test execution profiling/parallelism; C-03 Jest handle investigation; C-04 Nx 24 preparation; C-05 Ubuntu rollout; verified external-Desktop iOS test copy. C-06 policy clarification only if the owner selects it | 4–6 engineering days | Aim for15 min required checks while preserving test selection/counts/coverage. Clarify which workflows the current shared build context should require, then separately approve coordinated job-name/selector changes. Compare controlled CI runs, log runner/cache/tool versions and obtain a billing choice before additional macOS jobs. No paid Nx Cloud/new aggregate gate is presumed; an aggregate design can expand scope |
| F Structural client loading | W-01 endpoint-scoped injection and feature effect/provider boundaries | 7–12 engineering days | Remove an appropriate fraction of 251/225/540 KB raw emitted client contributions from initial bundles while retaining required auth/market/shell clients. Full metafile and waterfall parity plus first-screen regression; no wholesale removal or speed promise |

The recommended first selection is Wave A, then B. Wave A protects the meaning of the performance baseline: restoring real initial data can change render work, so speed comparisons must follow that repair. The full six-wave estimate is 25–42 engineering days; selecting a subset does not require committing to the whole roadmap. Small dead-code cleanup MOB-HEALTH-01 can be proposed separately rather than broaden a performance wave. Dependabot W-04 remains tracked until an upstream remedy or reachable tooling-cache exposure justifies a concrete change.

Unranked MOB-S11-02 address-cache refill, MOB-S11-04 Coil cache lifecycle, B007 rare overflow retention and B008 detached geocoding lifecycle need bounded characterization before implementation. The injected-client address characterization demonstrates repository refill but does not prove real HTTP cancellation failure or exposure. C-06 is a fifth unranked candidate: owner policy clarification precedes any coordinated gate change, and no merge incident is asserted. No new general harness, background framework, type layer or CI gate is included. A maintained Android Baseline Profile/Macrobenchmark or native performance CI would be a separate1–3day setup proposal plus device/runner cost, and requires approval. Exact-floor/device/archive/APNs/real-provider gaps are listed in coverage.

Mike's choices before implementation:

1. **Waves:** approve A only (recommended,4–7days), A+B (7–12days), or name another subset. Each approved wave becomes a separate backlog ticket and branch/PR after checking the current next ticket ID and latest master.
2. **Paging:** recommended interactive cap 100 after inventorying existing consumers and separating interactive endpoints from shared list/export consumers. Keep existing wire contracts coordinated with deployed clients. Cap200 aligns with some existing UI choices but has twice the row envelope. Merely raising Offset 500 enables existing deep-page links but retains increasingly expensive offset scans. A lower shared cap can break clients; coordinate any nonadditive policy with deployed TestFlight 13. For ordinary order pages, the proposed default is CreatedOn descending then Id descending; preserve explicit requested sorts and currency-leading financial order. Align the UI with supported depth. A new additive cursor or export path is an optional scope extension (roughly 1–3 additional engineering days for cursor design/implementation; an export subsystem is not estimated or included), not an implicit new feature.
3. **Initial JS:** select gzip9 estimate ceilings300 KiB customer,450 KiB partner,425 KiB admin (recommended) or choose others. Current307.62/499.80/449.06 KiB exceed those proposals. They are targets, not approval for a maintained CI gate.
4. **Native brand hold:** preserve the intentional1.8 s splash hold (default) or approve a product behavior change. Removing it changes presentation and cannot be disguised as an equivalent implementation optimization.
5. **iOS CI billing:** keep one macOS job initially and profile it (recommended first), or approve extra parallel macOS jobs after a costed comparison. Step medians alone do not predict end-to-end savings or billing.
6. **Devices and unavailable coverage:** continue simulator comparisons and explicit gaps (current choice), or later supply physical midrange devices for first-frame/DEV-network verdicts and approve distribution/provider tests separately. Exact iOS 16.0/API 26 and real Release archives cannot be claimed from nearby installed runtimes/Debug artifacts.
7. **Required-check policy, if Wave E is selected:** specify mandatory checks by PR class before approving distinct stable job names and matching hosted selectors. Retain strict checking. A new aggregate gate requires separate scope approval; no policy change is implicit in this audit.

Phase3 stops here. After a wave is selected, file only the approved scope, use one branch and PR per wave with one commit per cause, measure before/after the same way, run the applicable verification and obtain approval before merging. No deployment or DEV reset follows implicitly from wave approval.

Review covers scratch instrumentation only; no benchmarks, builds, host restarts, DB queries or external calls were executed by this review.\\n\\n## Request and trace cohorts\\n\\nHTTP total_ms measures loopback HTTP/1.1 headers plus body. ASP.NET Hosting Diagnostics RequestFinished elapsed is a separate server metric. Both include their stated instrumentation; EF-trace timings must stay separate from Hosting-Info-only timings. Root's existing setup parser QA correlated 180/180 durations with zero unparsable lines; it is setup fidelity, not a performance result.\\n\\nFor every main cohort require RequestFinished coverage equal to successful requests. Report pooled metrics and five per-run summaries; derive server per-run summaries from recorded run fields. For mobile sequences, group physical request statistics by endpoint path (excluding query values), then report the fixed serial launch request sum separately. The serial sum excludes pacing and native rendering/parallel scheduling.\\n\\nPreserve production rate limits. Report achieved physical request rate, ten synthetic identity partitions, warmups, 429/failure counts, encoding negotiation, response bytes and relevant cache/compression headers. Refresh private access sessions before their expiry; successful rotation is persisted per identity. Root is updating these scripts, so this lane makes no concurrent edits.\\n\\nSQL evidence must validate command scopes/log levels, record successful and failed EF events separately, and require nonempty commandText before using its hash as SQL proof. Zero EF commands under Hosting-Info-only logging is not zero DB work. PostgreSQL batch deltas include unrelated background work. Fixed split/projection queries are not a per-row N+1.\\n\\n## Broad page profile\\n\\nSource response shape is PagedData<T>(PageNumber,PageSize,Total,Data). The initial script recognizes Items, so root was notified to recognize the top-level Data array, retain total/page size, and validate returned count against min(limit,total) for this unfiltered admin scenario before running.\\n\\nLoopback and recorded-process checks, bounded response read, after-timer JSON decoding and client GC are appropriate for this separate profile. Reject an already-over-limit initial RSS before launching. The wall observer can close the client's socket; that does not prove all server work stops immediately, so confirm RequestFinished/settled work after an aborted cohort before continuing. Five-sample nearest-rank p90 is the maximum, descriptive only. RSS includes prior pools and retained heap, its 100ms sampling misses transient peaks, and sampling itself adds overhead. This profile can support an inefficient authenticated page-size finding; it does not establish public DoS.\\n\\n## Startup and logging\\n\\nStartup is process-cold with warm DB/disk caches. First /alive200 is a descriptive upper bound due to 250ms polling and sequential probe overhead. RSS at five seconds after all five hosts are alive is a shared cohort point, not five seconds after each individual readiness time. /alive is liveness, not first authenticated useful content. Root added the required first_alive timestamp completeness guard. Local macOS data does not predict Azure Linux worker startup.\\n\\nThe compiled logging harness compares actual five middleware with NullLogger and an identical direct delegate. Its allocations/CPU cost are isolated harness measurements, not server latency or GC pause measurements. Five runs and excluded warmups are required; true median is used. Privacy redaction and oversized-body suppression remain real guards.\\n\\n## Jobs and exceptional coverage\\n\\nJobs execute existing handlers in fresh scratch processes against exact CleansiaAuditJobs, guarded by owned Docker label plus loopback55432. Restore each specialty snapshot before each of five measured repetitions. Provider/factory HTTP guards throw and record attempts; providers_called=false is valid only with external_attempt_count=0. Queue recording captures namespaced requested queue and size/hash, never real transport. No Functions/IHostedService host is started. Trigger delivery, network latency and external success are excluded.\\n\\nModel/count setup is outside the timer; first handler lazy DI/JIT and instrumentation are inside. UTC is unmodified: specialty fixtures use SQL now(), so disclose actual occurrences, no-ops, failures and date-boundary effects. No frozen-clock substitution is made. Cancellation/provider attempts/wrong row deltas invalidate a run.\\n\\nB007 is optional unmeasured overflow work; the 500 newest notifications cap is explicit business intent. Completed T-0685 is a different, already fixed retention-enable issue. B008 is a conditional lifecycle/deduplication opportunity: its own scope refutes disposed-request-DbContext claims; ExecutionContext capture prevents asserting deterministic missing tenant. Tenant guard is fail-closed and no leak is established. These paths are not exercised by the primary fixture. No exact accepted/deferred duplicates for these mechanisms were found in owner plate, fix plan or backlog.\\n\\nRetention overflow, null-coordinate lifecycle, Respawner construction and test-provider disposal costs remain source-qualified or unresolved unless specifically measured. Do not promote them to performance findings. Existing unit/integration/HostTests and real provider/Functions trigger execution are separate coverage, owned/coordinated by root.\\n\\n## Browser peer review\\n\\nThe warm first-sample cache defect was reported and the peer corrected it with an excluded navigation in the same reused context. Document2xx is required and cohort warnings retain unexpected hosts/page errors. The explicit loopback HTTP/CONNECT proxy restricts exact DEV/local host-port targets, including literal IPs, and preserves HTTP cache. Qualify it as browser HTTP/CONNECT target isolation, not complete machine egress isolation. Normal Chromium HTTPS uses CONNECT; explicitly reject non-http absolute proxy schemes defensively if the proxy is changed. No browser run or external access was performed in this review.\\n\")"]
